container_info.reasoning: The project is focused on drafting and structuring documentation (static docs site). The container already includes documentation tooling such as mkdocs and sphinx, Node and static site toolchains, and Python (mkdocs) is lightweight and well-suited for headless container generation of documentation. MkDocs provides a minimal, file-based workflow (Markdown), built-in dev server, and simple build commands that match the lightweight/minimal requirements.
requirements: mkdocs (pip install mkdocs) - core static site generator
mkdocs-material or other minimal theme (optional but commonly used) (pip install mkdocs-material) — optional
git (already present) for source control and publishing
a minimal docs/ directory with Markdown files and mkdocs.yml config
mkdocs serve (dev) and mkdocs build (production) — use built-in server (no external web server)
small test: run `mkdocs build` to verify site builds without GUI
headless operation: ensure noninteractive environment variables (e.g., CI) and use file-based configuration; no DB or cache required
lightweight CI/test: pytest (optional) or simple scripts to validate presence of required Markdown files and successful mkdocs build

steps.name: Environment setup and verification (mkdocs CLI + safe pip installs + profile persistence)
steps.description: Verify python3, pip, git, curl/wget, and optional pytest exist. Confirm mkdocs CLI version (mkdocs --version) and Python import version; only install/upgrade mkdocs via sudo -H python3 -m pip when the CLI is missing or older than minimum (1.5.0). If MKDOCS_MATERIAL=1, check compatibility before installing mkdocs-material. Create an idempotent /etc/profile.d/mkdocs_env.sh that computes USER_BASE at login (no unresolved variables embedded) and ensures mkdocs-related user binaries will be on PATH for future shells. Operates in the workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation}"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "python3 not found" >&2; exit 2; }
python3 -m pip --version >/dev/null || { echo "pip for python3 not available" >&2; exit 3; }
command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "git not found" >&2; exit 4; }
if ! command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "neither curl nor wget present" >&2; exit 5
fi
MIN_MKDOCS="1.5.0"
# Get mkdocs CLI version if present, else 0
MK_CLI_VER=0
if command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  MK_CLI_VER=$(mkdocs --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /^[0-9]+\./){print $i; exit}}' || true)
fi
# Get importable mkdocs version (fallback)
MK_PY_VER=0
MK_PY_VER=$(python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
try:
    import mkdocs
    print(getattr(mkdocs,'__version__','0'))
except Exception:
    print('0')
PY
)
# Use packaging to compare versions (install via sudo if absent)
if ! python3 -c "import packaging.version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo -H python3 -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --no-input --quiet packaging || { echo 'failed to install packaging' >&2; exit 6; }
fi
is_old(){ python3 - <<PY
from packaging import version
import sys
v=sys.argv[1]
minv=sys.argv[2]
try:
    print(int(version.parse(v) < version.parse(minv)))
except Exception:
    print(1)
PY
"$1" "$2"
}
NEED_INSTALL=0
if [ "$MK_CLI_VER" = "0" ]; then
  # no cli, check import; if import also missing or too old, install
  if [ "$(is_old "$MK_PY_VER" "$MIN_MKDOCS")" -eq 1 ]; then
    NEED_INSTALL=1
  fi
else
  if [ "$(is_old "$MK_CLI_VER" "$MIN_MKDOCS")" -eq 1 ]; then
    NEED_INSTALL=1
  fi
fi
if [ $NEED_INSTALL -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "Installing/upgrading mkdocs (required >= $MIN_MKDOCS)"
  sudo -H python3 -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --no-input --upgrade "mkdocs>=$MIN_MKDOCS,<3" || { echo 'mkdocs install failed' >&2; exit 7; }
else
  echo "mkdocs ok: cli=$MK_CLI_VER py=$MK_PY_VER"
fi
# Optional mkdocs-material
if [ "${MKDOCS_MATERIAL:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  # check compatibility using installed mkdocs import
  python3 - <<PY || rc=$?; if [ "${rc:-0}" -ne 0 ]; then true; fi
from packaging import version
import sys
try:
    import mkdocs
    mv=version.parse(getattr(mkdocs,'__version__','0'))
except Exception:
    sys.exit(2)
# require mkdocs>=1.0 for material (conservative)
if mv < version.parse('1.0'):
    sys.exit(3)
sys.exit(0)
PY
  if [ ${rc:-0} -eq 0 ] || [ ${rc:-0} -eq 0 ]; then
    sudo -H python3 -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --no-input --upgrade mkdocs-material || echo 'mkdocs-material install failed' >&2
  else
    echo 'mkdocs-material incompatible; skipping' >&2
  fi
fi
# Create /etc/profile.d script that computes user base at login to avoid embedding UB_BIN
PROFILE_FILE=/etc/profile.d/mkdocs_env.sh
if [ -d /etc/profile.d ]; then
  if ! sudo test -f "$PROFILE_FILE" || ! sudo grep -q "# mkdocs environment - generated" "$PROFILE_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
    sudo tee "$PROFILE_FILE" >/dev/null <<'SH'
# mkdocs environment - generated
# At login compute user base and add its bin to PATH if present
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  USER_BASE=$(python3 -m site --user-base 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$USER_BASE" ] && [ -d "$USER_BASE/bin" ]; then
    case ":$PATH:" in
      *":$USER_BASE/bin:") :;;
      *) export PATH="$USER_BASE/bin:$PATH";;
    esac
  fi
fi
SH
    sudo chmod 644 "$PROFILE_FILE"
  fi
fi
# Final verification: ensure mkdocs CLI available on PATH
if ! command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo 'mkdocs CLI not available on PATH' >&2; exit 8
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation}"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
mkdir -p docs
[ -f docs/index.md ] && [ "${OVERWRITE:-0}" != "1" ] || cat > docs/index.md <<'MD'
# Welcome

This is a minimal MkDocs site for automated testing.
MD
[ -f docs/usage.md ] && [ "${OVERWRITE:-0}" != "1" ] || cat > docs/usage.md <<'MD'
# Usage

- mkdocs build
- mkdocs serve
MD
# Prefer material if importable
if python3 -c "import mkdocs_material" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  [ -f mkdocs.yml ] && [ "${OVERWRITE:-0}" != "1" ] || cat > mkdocs.yml <<'YML'
site_name: Documentation
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Usage: usage.md
theme:
  name: material
YML
else
  [ -f mkdocs.yml ] && [ "${OVERWRITE:-0}" != "1" ] || cat > mkdocs.yml <<'YML'
site_name: Documentation
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Usage: usage.md
YML
fi
# start.sh: derive WORKSPACE from env or script location; error if unset
cat > start.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${WORKSPACE-}"
if [ -z "${WORKSPACE:-}" ]; then
  # try derive from script location (parent dir)
  WORKSPACE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd || true)
  if [ -z "$WORKSPACE" ]; then
    echo 'WORKSPACE not set and could not be derived; set WORKSPACE to workspace path' >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi
cd "$WORKSPACE"
exec mkdocs serve --dev-addr=0.0.0.0:8000
SH
chmod +x start.sh
# build.sh: similar derivation
cat > build.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${WORKSPACE-}"
if [ -z "${WORKSPACE:-}" ]; then
  WORKSPACE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd || true)
  if [ -z "$WORKSPACE" ]; then
    echo 'WORKSPACE not set and could not be derived; set WORKSPACE to workspace path' >&2
    exit 2
  fi
fi
cd "$WORKSPACE"
mkdocs build --clean
SH
chmod +x build.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Testing scaffolding and lightweight checks (mkdocs build + optional pytest)
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation}"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Verify required files exist
[ -f docs/index.md ] || { echo 'missing docs/index.md' >&2; exit 6; }
[ -f mkdocs.yml ] || { echo 'missing mkdocs.yml' >&2; exit 7; }

# Ensure mkdocs CLI is available
if ! command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo 'mkdocs CLI not found on PATH' >&2
  exit 12
fi

# Run mkdocs build --clean
mkdocs build --clean || { echo 'mkdocs build failed' >&2; exit 8; }
[ -d site ] || { echo 'mkdocs build did not produce site/' >&2; exit 9; }
[ -f site/index.html ] || { echo 'site/index.html missing' >&2; exit 10; }

# If pytest available, create tests and run
if python3 -c "import pytest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mkdir -p tests
  cat > tests/test_mkdocs.py <<'PY'
import os
from pathlib import Path

def test_docs_and_site():
    base = os.environ.get('WORKSPACE') or os.getcwd()
    base = Path(base)
    assert (base / 'docs' / 'index.md').is_file()
    assert (base / 'mkdocs.yml').is_file()
    assert (base / 'site' / 'index.html').is_file()
PY
  # Run pytest with WORKSPACE env to make tests resilient
  WORKSPACE="$WORKSPACE" pytest -q || { echo 'pytest failed' >&2; exit 11; }
fi

# Success
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Canonical workspace from container information
WORKSPACE="/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation"
cd "$WORKSPACE"

# Verify mkdocs is available and has reasonable version
if ! command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "mkdocs CLI not found on PATH" >&2
  exit 12
fi

# Optionally enforce minimum version 1.5.0 if available
MIN_VER="1.5.0"
INST_VER="$(mkdocs --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' || true)"
if [ -n "$INST_VER" ]; then
  vercmp() { printf "%03d%03d%03d\n" $(echo "$1" | tr '.' ' '); }
  if [ "$(vercmp "$INST_VER")" -lt "$(vercmp "$MIN_VER")" ]; then
    echo "mkdocs version $INST_VER is older than required $MIN_VER" >&2
    exit 13
  fi
fi

# Run mkdocs build --clean
mkdocs build --clean || { echo 'mkdocs build failed' >&2; exit 11; }

Uses HTTP_CMD (curl or wget) consistently. Operates in the workspace: /tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/tmp/kavia/workspace/code-generation/documentation-drafting-session-236785-236786/Documentation}"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
mkdocs build --clean || { echo 'build failed' >&2; exit 12; }
[ -d site ] || { echo 'build failed: site/ missing' >&2; exit 13; }
LOG=/tmp/mkdocs_serve.log
: ${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT:=60}
# Choose HTTP_CMD
if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  HTTP_CMD="curl -sS -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 3 -o -"
elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  HTTP_CMD="wget -q -O - --server-response --timeout=3"
else
  echo 'neither curl nor wget available for validation' >&2; exit 14
fi
# Start server via start.sh in background process group
./start.sh >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$PID" | tr -d ' ')
exit_code=1
cleanup(){
  if kill -0 "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sleep 1
    kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}
trap 'cleanup; exit $exit_code' EXIT INT TERM
END=$((SECONDS+VALIDATION_TIMEOUT))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $END ]; do
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    BODY=$(curl -sS --max-time 3 -o - -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/ 2>/dev/null || true)
    HTTP_CODE=${BODY: -3}
    CONTENT=${BODY%???}
  else
    # wget: capture only body and hope for 200; fall back to checking non-empty
    CONTENT=$(wget -q -O - --timeout=3 http://127.0.0.1:8000/ 2>/dev/null || true)
    HTTP_CODE=200
  fi
  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ] && [ -n "${CONTENT:-}" ]; then
    echo "http_response_snippet:"
    echo "$CONTENT" | head -n 10
    exit_code=0
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
  echo 'server did not respond within timeout' >&2
  echo '--- mkdocs serve log (tail) ---'
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true
  exit_code=15
fi
# trap will cleanup and exit with $exit_code
